input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds Customer (our party) with a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months, worldwide ("in any territory"), covering any product or service that "competes with Vendor" — undefined scope with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (indeed it expressly bars acquisitions). That is squarely in walk-away territory under NONCOMPETE (post-term restriction longer than 12 months and undefined scope), so it fails both the preferred and the fallback positions. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. The smallest edit that reaches the preferred position is deletion of § 12.4, leaving § 12.3 to govern; we offer the narrowed fallback (single named product, in-term only, ≤12 months, with development and acquisition carve-outs) in the comment. No other provision restricts Customer's business — the only other competition reference (§ 24.2) restricts Vendor's assignment and benefits us.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or services we may develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted § 12.4 — a 24-month post-term, worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete is outside our playbook and also directly contradicts § 12.3, which confirms we have given no non-compete commitment. If the relationship genuinely needs protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to a single named competing product, during the term only and no more than 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month worldwide non-compete binding Customer in § 12.4.
